events.title: JavaScript ES3 standardized
events.summary: In December 1999, the ES3 standard was adopted — adding regular expressions, try/catch errors, and better string handling to JavaScript.
events.about: ES3 is the JavaScript the web ran on for a decade — the version every browser agreed on before ES5 and ES2015. It added regular expressions, try/catch exceptions, and clearer error rules, which made complex client-side apps (Gmail-era web apps, early Google Maps) possible.

narrative.whyChosen: ES3 was the stable JavaScript version the entire web learned and shipped for ten years.
narrative.whyImportant: Developers could finally validate text with regex and catch errors with try/catch — essential for Gmail-era web apps and early Google Maps.
narrative.problemSolved: Early JavaScript was too limited for complex client-side apps; websites needed better string tools and error handling without breaking old pages.
